questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
With reference to the two statements Assertion and Reason, choose the correct option.
Assertion: The order of reactivity towards S_N$1 reaction is: C_6$ H_5-$ CH_2$ Br > (CH_3$)_3-$ C$-$Br > (CH_3$)_2-$ CH$-$Br.
Reason: Among the given 3 compounds the Benzyl carbocation formed is the most stable while Isopropyl carbocation is the least stable one.
options: Both Assertion and Reason are correct and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are correct but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Reason is correct but Assertion is wrong
Assertion is correct but Reason is wrong
questions.solution:
The reactivity of alkyl halides towards $\text{S}_{\text{N}}1$ reactions depends on the stability of the intermediate carbocation formed during the rate-determining step.

The carbocations formed from the given alkyl halides are:
1. Benzyl carbocation ($\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{CH}_2^+$) from $\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{CH}_2\text{Br}$
2. tert-Butyl carbocation ($(\text{CH}_3)_3\text{C}^+$) from $(\text{CH}_3)_3\text{CBr}$
3. Isopropyl carbocation ($(\text{CH}_3)_2\text{CH}^+$) from $(\text{CH}_3)_2\text{CHBr}$

The benzyl carbocation is highly stabilized by the delocalization of the positive charge over the benzene ring through resonance. The tert-butyl carbocation is stabilized by hyperconjugation ($9\alpha$-hydrogens) and the +I effect of three methyl groups. The isopropyl carbocation is stabilized by hyperconjugation ($6\alpha$-hydrogens) and the +I effect of two methyl groups.

The resonance stabilization in the benzyl carbocation makes it the most stable among the three, while the isopropyl carbocation is the least stable.

Since the order of carbocation stability is Benzyl > tert-Butyl > Isopropyl, the order of reactivity towards $\text{S}_{\text{N}}1$ reaction follows the same trend: $\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{CH}_2\text{Br} > (\text{CH}_3)_3\text{CBr} > (\text{CH}_3)_2\text{CHBr}$.

Both the Assertion and the Reason are correct, and the Reason correctly explains the Assertion.

Answer: Both Assertion and Reason are correct and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion

questions.q: Identify the compounds A and B from the following reaction sequence:
questions.solution:
The final products of reductive ozonolysis of compound B are acetaldehyde ($\text{CH}_3\text{CHO}$) and 2-butanone ($\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COCH}_3$).

To find the structure of alkene B, we join the carbonyl carbons of the products with a double bond:
$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}=\text{O} + \text{O}=\text{C}(\text{CH}_3)\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3 \xrightarrow{\text{reconstruct}} \text{CH}_3\text{CH}=\text{C}(\text{CH}_3)\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$
Thus, B is 3-methylpent-2-ene.

Compound A undergoes dehydrohalogenation with alcoholic KOH to give B as the major product. According to Saytzeff's rule, the major product is the most substituted alkene.

Now check the given options for A:
In option (B), A is 3-bromo-3-methylpentane ($\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{C(Br)}(\text{CH}_3)\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$).
Dehydrohalogenation of 3-bromo-3-methylpentane yields two possible alkenes:
1. $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}=\text{C}(\text{CH}_3)\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$ (3-methylpent-2-ene) - more substituted, major product.
2. $\text{CH}_2=\text{C}(\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3)_2$ (2-ethylbut-1-ene) - less substituted, minor product.

Since the major product matches the structure of B, option (B) correctly identifies both A and B.

Answer:

questions.q: Identify the wrong statement from the following
options: The product formed when (–)–2–Methylbutan–1–ol is heated with Conc. HCl is (+)–1–Chloro–2–methylbutane with Retention of configuration
Vinyl halides do not undergo nucleophilic substitution reaction easily
$S_N1$ reaction of Alkyl halides is favoured by the presence of bulky substituents, protic solvents and the reaction products are a racemic mixture
$S_N2$ reaction of optically active halides are accompanied by Retention of configuration
questions.solution:
Option (A): The reaction of (–)–2–methylbutan–1–ol with conc. HCl involves the cleavage of the C–O bond at C1. The bonds attached to the chiral center at C2 are not broken, so the spatial arrangement (configuration) is retained. This statement is correct.

Option (B): Vinyl halides are highly unreactive towards nucleophilic substitution because the C–X bond acquires partial double bond character due to resonance, and the $sp^2$ hybridized carbon is less susceptible to nucleophilic attack. This statement is correct.

Option (C): $S_N1$ reactions are favored by bulky alkyl groups (which stabilize the carbocation and sterically hinder $S_N2$) and polar protic solvents. The carbocation intermediate is planar, allowing nucleophilic attack from both sides, which results in a racemic mixture. This statement is correct.

Option (D): $S_N2$ reactions of optically active halides proceed via a backside attack by the nucleophile. This leads to the inversion of configuration (Walden inversion), not retention. This statement is incorrect.

Answer: $S_N2$ reaction of optically active halides are accompanied by Retention of configuration

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Two statements, Assertion and Reason are given. With reference to them, choose the correct option.
Assertion: Hydrolysis of 2-Bromo-2-methylpropane follows $S_N1$ mechanism which involves 2 steps and the first step is:
The energy required to cleave C – Br is taken from the energy released due to Inductive effect and hyper-conjugative effect.
options: Assertion is correct but Reason is wrong
Both Assertion and Reason are correct but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are correct and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion
Reason is correct but Assertion is wrong
questions.solution:
The hydrolysis of 2-bromo-2-methylpropane (a tertiary alkyl halide) proceeds via the $S_N1$ mechanism.

The $S_N1$ mechanism is a two-step process. The first step is the slow, reversible cleavage of the C-Br bond to form a stable tertiary carbocation and a bromide ion. Thus, the Assertion is correct.

The energy required to break the C-Br bond is obtained from the solvation of the resulting ions (carbocation and halide ion) by the polar protic solvent. While inductive and hyperconjugative effects stabilize the intermediate carbocation, they do not provide the energy for the initial bond cleavage. Thus, the Reason is incorrect.

Therefore, the Assertion is correct but the Reason is wrong.

Answer: Assertion is correct but Reason is wrong

The reaction of ethylbenzene with excess $Cl_2$ in the presence of $hv$ (ultraviolet light) is a free radical substitution reaction. The reaction occurs at the benzylic position because the resulting benzylic radical is resonance-stabilized by the benzene ring.

The first step involves the abstraction of a hydrogen atom from the benzylic carbon (CH_2$) to form a 1-phenylethyl radical, which then reacts with $Cl_2$ to form 1-chloro-1-phenylethane.

Since the reagent $Cl_2$ is in excess, the reaction continues at the same benzylic position. questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Arrange the following compounds in the increasing order towards $\mathrm{S}_{\mathrm{N}} 1$ reactions.
questions.solution:
The rate of an $S_{N}1$ reaction depends on the stability of the carbocation intermediate formed after the departure of the leaving group (bromide ion). The more stable the carbocation, the faster the $S_{N}1$ reaction.

The carbocations formed from the given compounds are:
(I) Benzyl carbocation: $C_{6}H_{5}CH_{2}^{+}$, which is stabilized by resonance with one phenyl ring.
(II) Diphenylmethyl carbocation: $(C_{6}H_{5})_{2}CH^{+}$, which is stabilized by resonance with two phenyl rings.
(III) 1-Phenylethyl carbocation: $C_{6}H_{5}CH(CH_{3})^{+}$, which is stabilized by resonance with one phenyl ring and the inductive effect of the methyl group.
(IV) 1,1-Diphenylethyl carbocation: $(C_{6}H_{5})_{2}C(CH_{3})^{+}$, which is stabilized by resonance with two phenyl rings and the inductive effect of the methyl group.

Comparing the stabilities:
1. Compound (I) forms a primary benzylic carbocation (least stable among the options).
2. Compound (III) forms a secondary benzylic carbocation, which is more stable than (I) due to the electron-donating methyl group.
3. Compound (II) forms a secondary carbocation stabilized by two phenyl rings, which is more stable than (III).
4. Compound (IV) forms a tertiary carbocation stabilized by two phenyl rings and one methyl group, making it the most stable.

The order of stability of carbocations is (I) < (III) < (II) < (IV).

Therefore, the increasing order of reactivity towards $S_{N}1$ reactions is (I) < (III) < (II) < (IV).

Answer: I < III < II < IV

questions.q: Consider the following compounds , $\mathrm{CH}_3 \mathrm{Cl}(\mathrm{A}), \quad \mathrm{CH}_3 \mathrm{Br}(\mathrm{B}), \quad \mathrm{CH}_2 \mathrm{Br}_2(\mathrm{C}), \quad \mathrm{CHBr}_3(\mathrm{D})$ The correct order of boiling points of the compounds is:
questions.solution:
The boiling point of haloalkanes depends primarily on the molecular mass and the strength of intermolecular forces, specifically dipole-dipole interactions and London dispersion forces. As the molecular mass increases, the magnitude of van der Waals forces increases, leading to higher boiling points.

Comparing the compounds:
(A) $\mathrm{CH}_3\mathrm{Cl}$: Molecular mass $\approx 15 + 35.5 = 50.5$ u
(B) $\mathrm{CH}_3\mathrm{Br}$: Molecular mass $\approx 15 + 80 = 95$ u
(C) $\mathrm{CH}_2\mathrm{Br}_2$: Molecular mass $\approx 14 + 160 = 174$ u
(D) $\mathrm{CHBr}_3$: Molecular mass $\approx 13 + 240 = 253$ u

Since the molecular mass increases in the order $\mathrm{CH}_3\mathrm{Cl} < \mathrm{CH}_3\mathrm{Br} < \mathrm{CH}_2\mathrm{Br}_2 < \mathrm{CHBr}_3$, the boiling points follow the same trend. Therefore, the order is $\mathrm{D} > \mathrm{C} > \mathrm{B} > \mathrm{A}$.

Answer: D $>$ C $>$ B $>$ A

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following reaction can be used for the preparation of flouromethane?
questions.solution:
The preparation of alkyl fluorides from alkyl halides is typically achieved using the Swarts reaction. In this reaction, an alkyl bromide or alkyl chloride is treated with a metallic fluoride such as $\mathrm{AgF}$, $\mathrm{Hg}_2\mathrm{F}_2$, or $\mathrm{CoF}_2$.

The reaction is represented as: $\mathrm{CH}_3\mathrm{Br} + \mathrm{AgF} \rightarrow \mathrm{CH}_3\mathrm{F} + \mathrm{AgBr}$.

The other options are not suitable for the preparation of fluoromethane: $\mathrm{CH}_4 + \mathrm{F}_2$ is an extremely violent and uncontrolled free-radical substitution reaction, while $\mathrm{CH}_3\mathrm{OH} + \mathrm{HF}$ and $\mathrm{CH}_3\mathrm{NH}_2 + \mathrm{HF}$ do not undergo simple nucleophilic substitution to yield fluoromethane under standard laboratory conditions.

Answer: $\mathrm{CH}_3 \mathrm{Br}+\mathrm{AgF} \longrightarrow$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Choose the incorrect statement from the following.
options: $\mathrm{CH}_2 \mathrm{Cl}_2$ is widely used as a propellant in aerosols.
Freon 1, 2 is manufactured from trichloromethane by Swartz reaction
Antiseptic property of Iodoform is due to the liberation of $\mathrm{I}_2$ when it comes in contact with skin
DDT was widely used because of its effectiveness against mosquitos that spread malaria
questions.solution:
Dichloromethane ($\mathrm{CH}_2 \mathrm{Cl}_2$) is used as a solvent, a paint remover, as a propellant in aerosols, and as a process solvent in the manufacture of drugs. However, Freon 12 ($\mathrm{CCl}_2 \mathrm{F}_2$) is manufactured from tetrachloromethane ($\mathrm{CCl}_4$) by the Swarts reaction, not from trichloromethane ($\mathrm{CHCl}_3$). Therefore, the statement that Freon 1, 2 is manufactured from trichloromethane by the Swarts reaction is incorrect.

Iodoform ($\mathrm{CHI}_3$) acts as an antiseptic due to the liberation of free iodine when it comes in contact with the skin, not due to the substance itself. DDT (p,p'-dichlorodiphenyltrichloroethane) was indeed used extensively to control malaria-carrying mosquitoes and typhus-carrying lice.

Answer: Freon 1, 2 is manufactured from trichloromethane by Swartz reaction

The reaction sequence starts with the diazotization of aniline: $\mathrm{C}_6 \mathrm{H}_5 \mathrm{NH}_2 + \mathrm{NaNO}_2 + 2\mathrm{HCl} \xrightarrow{0^{\circ} \mathrm{C}} \mathrm{C}_6 \mathrm{H}_5 \mathrm{N}_2^{+} \mathrm{Cl}^{-} + \mathrm{NaCl} + 2\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}$. questions.q: Identify the incorrect statement.
options: The reaction of $\mathrm{C}_6 \mathrm{H}_5 \mathrm{CH}_2-\mathrm{CHCl}-\mathrm{C}_6 \mathrm{H}_5$ with alc. KOH on heating yields two products.
When (-)-2-bromooctane is reacted with aqueous KOH , the substitution follows $\mathrm{S}_{\mathrm{N}} 2$ mechanism and product formed is $(-)$-Octan-2-ol.
Benzylic halides show higher reactivity towards $S_N 1$ reaction.
Optically active (-)-2-Methylbutan-1-ol on reaction with HCl yields a product $(+)$-1-Chloro-2-methylbutane.
questions.solution:
(1) Correct: Dehydrohalogenation of $C_6H_5CH_2-CHCl-C_6H_5$ with alc. KOH gives stilbene (C_6H_5-CH=CH-C_6H_5$), which exists as two geometric isomers (cis and trans) — hence two products.

(2) Incorrect: $S_N2$ involves Walden inversion. Reaction of $(-)$-2-bromooctane with aqueous KOH via $S_N2$ gives $(+)$-octan-2-ol (inverted configuration), not $(-)$-octan-2-ol.

(3) Correct: Benzylic halides readily undergo $S_N1$ because the benzylic carbocation intermediate is stabilised by resonance with the benzene ring.

(4) Correct: Reaction of $(-)$-2-methylbutan-1-ol with HCl replaces $-OH$ at the primary carbon $C_1$. No bond at the chiral centre $C_2$ is broken, so configuration is retained. However the sign of optical rotation changes, giving $(+)$-1-chloro-2-methylbutane.

The incorrect statement is (2).$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Toluene when reacted with $\mathrm{Cl}_2$ gas at 385 K forms a product X which undergoes further reaction with Sodium ethoxide to yield product Y. The structure of Y is ____。
questions.solution:
Toluene (C_6H_5CH_3$) reacts with $Cl_2$ gas at 385 K (which is a high temperature, often associated with free radical substitution) to form benzyl chloride (C_6H_5CH_2Cl$).

The reaction is: $C_6H_5CH_3 + Cl_2 \xrightarrow{385 K}$ C_6H_5CH_2Cl + HCl$.

Benzyl chloride (C_6H_5CH_2Cl$) then reacts with sodium ethoxide (NaOCH_2CH_3$), which is a strong nucleophile, via an $S_N2$ mechanism to form benzyl ethyl ether (C_6H_5CH_2OCH_2CH_3$).

The reaction is: $C_6H_5CH_2Cl + NaOCH_2CH_3 \rightarrow C_6H_5CH_2OCH_2CH_3 + NaCl$.

The structure of the product Y is benzyl ethyl ether, which corresponds to the fourth structure provided in the options.

Answer:

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which one of the following is a true statement with reference to reaction between 2- Bromo-2-methylpropane and aqueous KOH ?
options: The reaction is not favoured by the presence of polar protic solvent.
The reaction occurs at a slow rate since it follows $\mathrm{S}_{\mathrm{N}} 2$ mechanism.
The reaction occurs at a fast rate since the substrate is a tertiary alkyl halide and follows $\mathrm{S}_{\mathrm{N}} 1$ mechanism.
The rate of reaction depends on the concentration of the haloalkane and the nucleophile $\mathrm{OH}^{-}$
questions.solution:
The substrate 2-bromo-2-methylpropane is a tertiary alkyl halide. Tertiary alkyl halides undergo nucleophilic substitution primarily via the $\mathrm{S}_{\mathrm{N}}1$ mechanism because the carbocation intermediate formed is highly stable due to inductive and hyperconjugation effects.

The $\mathrm{S}_{\mathrm{N}}1$ mechanism involves the rate-determining step of carbocation formation, which is independent of the concentration of the nucleophile. Thus, the rate law is given by $\text{Rate} = k[\text{Substrate}]$.

Polar protic solvents stabilize the carbocation intermediate and the leaving group through solvation, thereby facilitating the $\mathrm{S}_{\mathrm{N}}1$ reaction.

Comparing the options, the statement that the reaction occurs at a fast rate because the substrate is a tertiary alkyl halide following the $\mathrm{S}_{\mathrm{N}}1$ mechanism is correct, as the stability of the tertiary carbocation allows for a relatively rapid formation compared to primary or secondary substrates in the same mechanism.

Answer: The reaction occurs at a fast rate since the substrate is a tertiary alkyl halide and follows $\mathrm{S}_{\mathrm{N}} 1$ mechanism.

questions.q: Which of the following haloalkanes will give more than one isomeric product, on being heated with alc. KOH ?
questions.solution:
Dehydrohalogenation of haloalkanes with alcoholic KOH follows Saytzeff rule, where the major product is the more substituted alkene. If multiple distinct $\beta$-hydrogens are available such that different alkenes can be formed, isomeric products are obtained.

For 1-chloro-2-methylbutane (CH_3CH_2CH(CH_3)CH_2Cl$), the only \beta$-hydrogen is on the carbon at position 2, leading to 2-methyl-1-butene. Only one product is formed.

For 2-chlorobutane (CH_3CH_2CHClCH_3$), \beta$-hydrogens are present on C1 and C3. Elimination from C1 gives but-1-ene, and elimination from C3 gives but-2-ene (cis and trans isomers). Thus, multiple isomeric products are formed.

For 2-chloro-3,3-dimethylpentane (CH_3CHClC(CH_3)_2CH_2CH_3$), \beta$-hydrogens are present on C1 and C3. However, C3 has no hydrogens, so elimination can only occur towards C1, yielding 3,3-dimethylpent-2-ene. Only one product is formed.

For 1-chloropentane (CH_3CH_2CH_2CH_2CH_2Cl$), the only \beta$-hydrogen is on C2, leading to pent-1-ene. Only one product is formed.

Answer: 2- Chlorobutane.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Both reactions (i) and (ii) give the same compound X as the major product. Identify X
(i). 3-Methylbut-1-ene $+\mathrm{HCl} \rightarrow \mathrm{X}$
(ii). Neopentyl alcohol $+\mathrm{HCl}\left(\right.$ anh. $\left.\mathrm{ZnCl}_2\right) \rightarrow \mathrm{X}$
questions.solution:
In reaction (i), the electrophilic addition of $\mathrm{HCl}$ to 3-methylbut-1-ene proceeds via the formation of a carbocation. The initial protonation of the double bond yields the secondary carbocation $(CH_3)_2CH-CH^{+}-CH_3$. This secondary carbocation undergoes a 1,2-hydride shift to form the more stable tertiary carbocation $(CH_3)_2C^{+}-CH_2-CH_3$. Subsequent attack by the chloride ion gives the major product $X$ as 2-chloro-2-methylbutane, which is $(CH_3)_2CCl-CH_2-CH_3$.

In reaction (ii), the reaction of neopentyl alcohol $(CH_3)_3C-CH_2OH$ with $\mathrm{HCl}$ and anhydrous $\mathrm{ZnCl}_2$ (Lucas reagent) involves the formation of a carbocation. The protonated alcohol loses water to form the primary neopentyl carbocation $(CH_3)_3C-CH_2^{+}$. This primary carbocation is highly unstable and undergoes a 1,2-methyl shift to rearrange into the more stable tertiary carbocation $(CH_3)_2C^{+}-CH_2-CH_3$. The chloride ion then attacks this tertiary carbocation to yield the same major product $X$, which is 2-chloro-2-methylbutane, $(CH_3)_2CCl-CH_2-CH_3$.

Answer: $\left(\mathrm{CH}_3\right)_2-\mathrm{CCl}_{-}-\mathrm{CH}_2-\mathrm{CH}_3$

Finally, the hydrolysis of the nitrile $[Y]$ with excess dilute $HCl$ converts the $-CN$ group into a carboxylic acid group $-COOH$. Thus, the final product $[Z]$ is 2-(4-chlorophenyl)acetic acid, which corresponds to the structure shown in the first option.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Choose the incorrect statement from the following.
options: Carbon tetrachloride is used as a preservative for anatomical specimens
Dichloromethane is used as a solvent in drug industry
Freon-12 acts as a propellant in aerosol sprays
DDT is useful to protect crops and to kill mosquitoes that spread malaria
questions.solution:
Carbon tetrachloride is primarily used as a solvent for oils, fats, lacquers, varnishes, rubber waxes, and resins. It is also used as a fire extinguisher under the name Pyrene. It is not used as a preservative for anatomical specimens; formaldehyde is commonly used for that purpose.

Dichloromethane is widely used as a solvent in the pharmaceutical industry, as a paint remover, as a propellant in aerosols, and as a process solvent in the manufacture of drugs.

Freon-12 (dichlorodifluoromethane) is a chlorofluorocarbon used as a refrigerant and as a propellant in aerosol sprays.

DDT (p,p'-dichlorodiphenyltrichloroethane) was widely used as an insecticide to protect crops and to control mosquitoes that spread malaria and lice that carry typhus.

Answer: Carbon tetrachloride is used as a preservative for anatomical specimens

Option (4): Tertiary alkyl halide — $S_N2$ is sterically hindered; proceeds via $S_N1$ instead.

The compound that undergoes $S_N2$ with retention of configuration is option (1).

$t$-butyl chloride is a tertiary alkyl halide, represented as $(CH_{3})_{3}CCl$.

In nucleophilic substitution reactions, tertiary alkyl halides are highly sterically hindered, which prevents the approach of a nucleophile from the backside, making the $\mathrm{S}_{\mathrm{N}}2$ mechanism extremely slow or unfavorable.

Conversely, the carbocation formed after the departure of the chloride ion, $(CH_{3})_{3}C^{+}$, is a tertiary carbocation, which is highly stabilized by the inductive effect and hyperconjugation of the nine surrounding hydrogen atoms.

Due to the formation of a stable intermediate carbocation and the steric hindrance at the reaction center, $t$-butyl chloride undergoes hydrolysis primarily through the $\mathrm{S}_{\mathrm{N}}1$ mechanism.

Answer: $\mathrm{S}_{\mathrm{N}} 1$ mechanism

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Alkyl halides undergoing $\mathrm{S}_{\mathrm{N}} 2$ reaction do inverse
questions.solution:
The $\mathrm{S}_{\mathrm{N}}2$ reaction mechanism involves a concerted process where the nucleophile attacks the electrophilic carbon atom from the side opposite to the leaving group.

This backside attack leads to the transition state where the nucleophile and the leaving group are partially bonded to the central carbon atom.

As the leaving group departs, the configuration of the chiral center is inverted, similar to an umbrella turning inside out in the wind. This phenomenon is known as the Walden inversion.

Therefore, the $\mathrm{S}_{\mathrm{N}}2$ reaction proceeds with complete inversion of configuration.

Answer: inversion of configuration

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the product is not possible in Wurtz reaction?
questions.solution:
The Wurtz reaction involves the coupling of two alkyl halide molecules in the presence of sodium metal and dry ether to form a symmetrical alkane with an even number of carbon atoms.

The general reaction is $2RX + 2Na \rightarrow R-R + 2NaX$.

Since the reaction involves the combination of two alkyl groups, the resulting alkane must contain at least two carbon atoms (if methyl halides are used) or an even number of carbon atoms if higher alkyl halides are used. Specifically, the product $R-R$ will always have an even number of carbon atoms if $R$ is an alkyl group derived from a single type of alkyl halide.

Methane (CH_4$) contains only one carbon atom. It is impossible to form a single carbon alkane through the coupling of two alkyl groups in a Wurtz reaction, as the minimum number of carbons in the product is two (ethane).

Ethane (C_2H_6$), Propane (C_3H_8$), and Butane (C_4H_{10}$) can be formed under specific conditions (e.g., mixing different alkyl halides for propane, or using ethyl halides for butane). Methane cannot be formed.

Answer: Methane
